explanations: The parser decodes every incoming Buffer on its own with chunk.toString("utf8"). Chunk boundaries fall at arbitrary byte offsets, so a multi-byte UTF-8 character such as "ó" (2 bytes) or "龍" (3 bytes) is sometimes split between two chunks. Each half is invalid on its own and decodes to U+FFFD replacement characters, which are still valid JSON, so the corrupted name goes into the totals as a different artist. Small files arrive as one chunk and never hit this, and ASCII names can't be split. The fix keeps a StringDecoder for the life of the stream. decoder.write() holds back an incomplete trailing character until the next chunk, and _flush adds decoder.end(). Carrying the partial line in `carry` handles lines that span chunks, and the decoder does the same for characters.
